rationale: Pontiff and Woodgate (2008, Journal of Finance), 'Share Issuance and Cross-sectional Returns'. Empirical cross-sectional paper using CRSP (shares outstanding, returns, market equity) and Compustat (book equity, data60) for January 1970 to December 2003 (2,494,343 firm-month observations; 2,155,945 in the Table III regression sample), plus a pre-1970 out-of-sample CRSP period September 1932 to December 1969 (568,449 firm-months; 373,590 in the Table VI regression sample). Methodology is fully operationalized: split-adjusted share issuance via CRSP's factor-to-adjust-shares (equations 1-3), Fama-MacBeth monthly cross-sectional regressions with five holding periods (1-month, 6-month, year-1, year-2, year-3 returns), Pontiff (1996) overlap-consistent t-statistics, 1% winsorization of regressors, and explicitly defined control variables (BM, ME, MOM) with dummy variables for missing data. Tables I, III, V, VI report numerical results replicable from CRSP+Compustat. Two tables (II and IV) require Thomson SDC Platinum event data (SEOs, repurchases, stock mergers) which is not available in ClickHouse; these are excluded from the replication scope but do not block the headline results (Tables I, III) or the out-of-sample evidence (Tables V, VI). One data caveat: pre-1970 book equity comes from Ken French / Davis-Fama-French (2000), not Compustat — BM rows in Tables V/VI may be unavailable, while all CRSP-only rows (ISSUE, DT-ISSUE, ME, MOM) remain replicable.
